conclusion.quantifiers: forall fixed C>0, exists N_C, forall integers n>=N_C

PO1-RATIO-ALGEBRA: Thus rho_C(n)=u_n(C)/F_n=K_C [n^2/(n+0.515)^2][log^2(n+e)/n^(1/3)], where K_C=C(0.8274)^2/4. The constants 0.515 and 0.8274 are unchanged and C is independent of n.
PO2-ELEMENTARY-LIMIT: Let t_n=(1/3)log(n+e). Then t_n tends to infinity and (n+e)^(1/3)=exp(t_n).
The identity log^2(n+e)/n^(1/3)=9[(n+e)/n]^(1/3)t_n^2 exp(-t_n) is exact.
For n>=1, [(n+e)/n]^(1/3)<=(1+e)^(1/3). Since exp(t)>=t^3/6 for t>0 by the positive exponential series, 0<=9t_n^2 exp(-t_n)<=54/t_n.
Therefore 0<=log^2(n+e)/n^(1/3)<=54(1+e)^(1/3)/t_n, and the upper bound tends to zero. The squeeze theorem proves the limit.
PO3-FIXED-C-QUANTIFIER: For an arbitrary fixed C>0, K_C is a finite positive constant and 0<n^2/(n+0.515)^2<1, so PO2 gives rho_C(n)->0.
For n>=3, n+e<=2n and log(n+e)<=log(2n)<=2log n. Hence rho_C(n)=O_C(log^2(n)/n^(1/3)).
By the limit definition, for this fixed C there exists N_C such that every integer n>=N_C satisfies rho_C(n)<1. No cutoff uniform over unbounded C is asserted.
PO4-FLOOR-CHAIN: Because U_JY(n)=max(log 2,n-1,F_n), one has F_n<=U_JY(n); because z<=ceil(z) for every real z, U_JY(n)<=ceil(U_JY(n)).
PO5-SUFFICIENT-SEARCH-BOUND: The previously proved strict-search family starts at m_0=ceil(U_JY(n)); hence tilde_m_JY(n,epsilon)>=ceil(U_JY(n)) for every epsilon>0 in that family. Its computable-input implementation is stated for positive rational epsilon, but the floor inequality itself is the defining start constraint and does not use epsilon magnitude.
PO6-EXPONENTIATION: PO4 and PO5 give u_n(C)<tilde_m_JY(n,epsilon). Strict monotonicity of exp yields Y_n(C)=exp(u_n(C))<exp(tilde_m_JY(n,epsilon))=tilde_M_JY(n,epsilon).
PO7-SCOPE: Only eventual incompatibility of the current sufficient certificate floor with the fixed-C diagonal is proved. No statement about the actual natural-order remainder below U_JY, other sufficient moduli, internal prefixes, Li coefficients, or RH follows.
